## Context / Problem
Gerrit change 1757 (merged as 065af7c163, ticket small-delicious-loris) taught rebar._store.sync._union_merge to recover ONE merge-abort class: untracked files origin wants to create ("untracked working tree files would be overwritten by merge") — quarantine the named paths, retry once. The second proven abort class, variant (b), remains unhandled: tracked files with local working-tree changes — in practice deletions of tracked per-ticket artifacts left by an interrupted compaction fold — make `git merge origin/tickets` abort with "Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge". The abort leaves reconverge unable to advance and strands local ticket commits off origin (live recurrence recorded on e72e-259d-5ee7-4e73: 119 tracked `.archived` deletions wedged the store). Sibling story untrack-runtime-markers removes the marker sub-class at its source, but an interrupted fold can still leave tracked EVENT-file deletions (compact_txn renames sources to `*.retired` — a rename of a tracked file is a tracked deletion + an untracked creation), so reconverge must self-heal this class regardless.

## Approach
Extend the recovery seam 1757 added in src/rebar/_store/sync.py: on merge failure, additionally detect the "Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge" signature and parse the paths git names (same parsing pattern as the merged `_untracked_overwrite_paths`). For each named path, act by its status: a working-tree DELETION of a tracked file (`git status --porcelain` reports ` D`) is restored non-destructively via `git checkout -- <path>` (content already at HEAD — nothing can be lost); a working-tree MODIFICATION is first copied into the same quarantine directory 1757 established (`<git-common-dir>/reconverge-quarantine/<utc-ts>/`) and then restored via `git checkout -- <path>` (the local bytes are preserved in quarantine, the HEAD bytes unblock the merge). Then retry the merge once. Any other failure — including a genuine index/content conflict — keeps today's behavior exactly: `git merge --abort`, keep local, hint `rebar fsck-recover`. Positive rationale: this reuses the exact recovery shape already reviewed and merged for variant (a) (parse-what-git-names, move-never-delete, single retry, fall back to abort), extending one proven seam rather than adding a second recovery mechanism.

## Scope
- src/rebar/_store/sync.py — detect + parse the local-changes abort; restore/quarantine the named paths; single retry.
- tests/unit/test_store_sync_reconverge.py — extend the 1757 test module with RED-first coverage for variant (b): tracked-deletion fixture and tracked-modification fixture.

## Testing
- RED first: fixture tracker where HEAD tracks a file, the worktree deletes it, and origin/tickets modifies it; assert the union merge currently aborts and HEAD is un-merged, for the local-changes reason specifically.
- GREEN: same fixture after the fix — merge completes with both parents, the local-only commit stays reachable, the deleted file is back at its merged content.
- Modification path: worktree-modified tracked file named by the abort — quarantine copy exists with the local bytes, merge completes.
- Guard: a genuine content conflict (both sides commit different content) still aborts and keeps local (unchanged behavior); `.tmp-event-*` and paths git does not name are untouched.
- Mutation check: skipping the restore step returns the RED assertion.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A reconverge whose union merge aborts only on local changes to tracked store-artifact paths now completes keeping both parents, with no local commit orphaned; checked by the new RED-to-GREEN tests.
- [x] A worktree modification named by the abort is preserved byte-for-byte in the quarantine directory before restore; checked by test comparing quarantined bytes.
- [x] A genuine merge conflict still aborts, keeps local, and hints fsck-recover; checked by the guard test.
- [x] [operator-attested] `make lint` and `make typecheck` clean; lands via Gerrit (LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1) before close.
